questions.question: A lounge suite has a cash price of R11 999. The HP deal asks a 10% deposit and 24 monthly instalments of R589,50. Calculate the total HP price and the extra paid compared with cash, and explain how lay-by would differ for the same suite.
questions.expected_answer: The deposit is 10% of 11 999, which is R1 199,90. The instalments total 589,50 × 24 = R14 148,00. The total HP price is deposit plus instalments: 1 199,90 + 14 148,00 = R15 347,90. The extra paid for buying on HP is 15 347,90 − 11 999 = R3 348,90, nearly 28% above the cash price — this extra is the interest and charges of the agreement, and until the final instalment the store still owns the suite. Lay-by charges no interest: the buyer pays the exact cash price of R11 999 in instalments, about R2 000 a month over six months, but only receives the suite once the final payment is made. HP sells immediate possession at a premium; lay-by sells the cash price in exchange for waiting.

questions.question: A car priced at R189 900 is financed with a deposit of R18 990, 60 monthly repayments of R3 499 and a balloon payment of R56 970. Calculate the total cost of the deal, state how much more than the price this is, and explain both why the instalment looks affordable and what the owner's options are when the balloon falls due.
questions.expected_answer: The repayments total 3 499 × 60 = R209 940. The full cost is deposit plus repayments plus balloon: 18 990 + 209 940 + 56 970 = R285 900, which is 285 900 − 189 900 = R96 000 more than the windscreen price. The instalment looks affordable because the balloon pushes R56 970 of the debt — 30% of the price — to the end of the term, so the monthly payments only carry the remaining debt and are therefore lower than an ordinary loan's would be. When month sixty arrives the balloon must still be dealt with, in one of three ways: pay the R56 970 as a lump sum, refinance it into a new loan and pay new interest on old debt, or sell the car to settle it. The deal should be judged on the total of everything ever paid, not on the monthly figure.

questions.question: A R25 000 personal loan runs 36 months at R1 095 per month, with a R69 monthly service fee and a R1 207,50 initiation fee. Calculate the total cost of credit. Then, for a car policy with a R4 500 excess, calculate the payout on damage of R28 600 and explain what the excess is for.
questions.expected_answer: The true monthly outflow is 1 095 + 69 = R1 164. The total paid is the initiation fee plus 36 months of that outflow: 1 207,50 + 36 × 1 164 = 1 207,50 + 41 904 = R43 111,50. The total cost of credit is everything paid minus the cash received: 43 111,50 − 25 000 = R18 111,50, which is over 72% of the amount borrowed — every fee counts, not only the advertised repayment. On the insurance claim, the insurer pays the damage minus the excess: 28 600 − 4 500 = R24 100, while the owner pays the first R4 500 personally. The excess keeps small claims out of the system, which keeps premiums lower for everyone, and it gives the owner a reason to avoid careless small losses; on a financed car the bank usually requires this insurance because the car is its security until the debt, including any balloon, is settled.
